newsitem.title: USA: Evans completes new credit facility.
newsitem.headline: Evans completes new credit facility.

text.p: Evans Inc, a fur and apparel retail chain, said Wednesday it completed a new, three-year, $27.0-million credit facility to refinance its existing $22.5 million working capital and term financing agreement.
Under the new agreement, Evans said it will have a $25.0 million revolving line of credit and a $2.0 million term loan.
The credit facility is with Jackson National Life Co.
All assets and properties will be pledged as security for the new credit facility, Evans said.

Earlier, Evans reported a loss for fiscal 1997 ended March 1 of $4.7 million or $0.96 a share, compared with a profit of $234,000 or $0.05 a share in fiscal 1996. Fiscal 1996 results included a $0.15 a share charge.
Revenues for the year declined to $69.8 million from $82.7 million.

"The difficulty this past year is primarily owed to the unprecedented rise in worldwide wholesale fur prices, principally mink, to new record levels this past year," Patrick Regan, president, said in a statement. "Average wholesale mink prices soared by over 60 percent."
He added that growth in fur sales at higher retail prices was "excellent," but not sufficient to offset the drop in fur sales in the more moderate price category.

"We have recently realigned responsibilities and reduced costs throughout the corporation, which is expected to save nearly $3,100,000 in fiscal 1998 alone," Regan added. "We are also encouraged by the recent easing of mink prices and expect to be in a much improved position to secure sufficient quantities of fur garments at all retail price levels to meet our needs in the coming season."
